narrative:
I submitted an ACH deposit through Bitstamp, a cryptocurrency trading platform. Bitstamp advertises instant ACH credits and immediately reflected the deposit in my account balance. However, when I attempted to access or withdraw the funds, I was informedafter the factthat the funds would be locked for seven business days until my bank confirmed the debit.

At no point during the deposit process was this restriction disclosed. There was no warning, no disclaimer, and no indication that the funds would be held once credited. The user interface, confirmation screen, and deposit window all give the impression that the funds are available for immediate usenot locked behind an arbitrary, undisclosed holding period. 

This is a classic case of bait-and-switch. Bitstamp lures users into initiating deposits under the impression of full liquidity, only to freeze the funds after the transaction completes. I would not have authorized the deposit had I known the funds would be restricted. 

When I contacted Bitstamp support, I requested that they either release the funds or reverse the ACH transfer so the money could be returned to my bank account. They refused, offering only a generic explanation about their internal policy and stating that I must wait for my bank to respondeven though the funds were credited instantly and no fraud or bank issue was present. 

I believe this conduct : Constitutes deceptive advertising and a failure to disclose material limitations ; Deprives consumers of control over their funds ; Creates unjust enrichment by forcing users into a locked system under false pretenses ; And may violate provisions of the Electronic Fund Transfer Act and UDAP standards under the CFPBs authority.

Resolution Requested : 1. Immediate release of my funds or reversal of the ACH transaction ; 2. Clear, prominent disclosures on Bitstamps platform regarding withdrawal restrictions before a user initiates a deposit ; 3. sub_issue: An existing modification, forbearance plan, short sale, or other loss mitigation relief
narrative:
We are VA loan holders with Freedom Mortgage, Loan # XXXX. After a major loss of income in XX/XX/XXXX, we requested a 3-month forbearance. We were told repeatedly by multiple representatives that at the end of the forbearance, we could do a simple loan modification that would add the missed payments to the back of the loan with no changes to our loan terms or interest rate. At no point was it disclosed that this would alter our interest rate. 

When the original forbearance ended in XX/XX/XXXX, we called and were told we would receive VA trial payment documents within 3 weeks but we never did. In XXXX, a representative confirmed that the trial modification was never submitted properly and instead offered a second 3-month forbearance beginning in XXXX. We were also told not to make a payment for XXXX, as it would not apply correctly and instead would go toward XXXX. They explicitly instructed us to let XXXX go unpaid and begin a new forbearance in XXXX. 

Once again, we were told that we could do a loan modification at the end of the forbearance to add the missed payments to the back of the loan and again, no mention was made of any change to our interest rate. Based on this, we accepted the new forbearance as a way to recover financially, and planned to resume full payments starting XX/XX/XXXX. 

As of XX/XX/XXXX, we are ready to resume payments in full. However, when we called to proceed with the trial modification, we were told that our only option is a modification that would increase our interest rate from 2.25 % to over 7 %. This is a complete reversal of what we were told, and a major omission of material terms. 

We have spoken with multiple Freedom Mortgage representatives over the last several months, and not one of them disclosed that our interest rate would change as part of the modification process. This has had a direct impact on our financial planning, and we would never have agreed to a forbearance under these terms had we been fully informed. 

We are currently escalating the issue and have requested that Freedom Mortgage pull the call recordings. A supervisor acknowledged that this was mishandled but claimed that theres nothing we can do aside from retraining the employee. That response is unacceptable. We should have been clearly informed : You will be able to modify at the end of the forbearance ; however, your interest rate may change. That was never communicated. 

We are requesting that the CFPB assist in ensuring the following : That the modification proceeds as originally stated, with no change to our 2.25 % VA loan interest rate. 

That Freedom Mortgage is held accountable for its failure to disclose material terms related to a federally-backed loan modification. 

That all call recordings be reviewed for compliance with the Truth in Lending Act and CFPBs Mortgage Servicing Rules. 

This has caused undue stress and confusion for our family and could have been entirely avoided had the information been properly disclosed from the beginning.

This pattern of abuse is consistent with prior cases including * * Robinson v. Nationstar ( 2023 WL 3138203 ) * *, * * Campbell v. Nationstar * *, and * * McGinnis v. Nationstar * *, which demonstrate a repeated pattern of misconduct.

I am submitting this complaint because XXXX XXXX XXXX  has continued to re-age a delinquent account in violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 5 ) ). By failing to do soand continuing to update the account as recently delinquentXXXX XXXX is misrepresenting the age of the debt, which is prohibited re-aging and a violation of 15 U.S.C. 1681s2 ( a ) ( 5 ).

Your own reporting reflects delinquency as early as XX/XX/XXXX, showing 30-day, 60-day, and 90-day missed payments through that year.

I never made any payments on this account, and it has never been brought current.

You have continued to report 180-day delinquencies every year from XXXX through XXXX without basis. 
Under FCRA 605 ( a ), the 7-year time limit for reporting delinquent information begins with the first missed payment that was never resolved. In this case, the Date of First Delinquency is no later than XX/XX/XXXX, meaning this account must be purged by XX/XX/XXXX. 
Your continued reporting past this date without proof of repayment, reinvestigation, or consumer authorization is a clear violation of federal law.

Additionally, under FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 5 ), re-aging a tradeline to make it appear more recent is unlawful without actual payment or consumer activity.

Under FCRA 605B, you were notified of identity theft and presented with proper documentation. You have failed to block the item as required and failed to provide any factual basis for denial.

Under the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act, Tenn. Code 47-18-104, these continued practices may also constitute deceptive and unfair reporting in commerce.

narrative:
AvantCard / XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX : Complaint Against AvantCard ( XXXX ) Unfair Monthly Fee Imposed Amid Disputes and Financial Hardship I am filing a formal complaint against AvantCard issued by XXXX regarding a newly imposed $ XXXX ( {$100.00} annual ) fee on my credit card account, which I never agreed to when opening the account. I was recently notified that this fee will be added beginning XX/XX/year>, unless I opt out but doing so results in account closure. 

This action is highly concerning for the following reasons : I am currently experiencing financial hardship and have had multiple active disputes across credit lines. Avant acknowledges my payment and utilization history in their notice, yet fails to recognize that many of the negative data points relate to ongoing or previously submitted disputes. 

Some items remain marked on my credit reports as " Account information disputed by consumer '' ; yet Avant is weaponizing these data points to justify new fees instead of offering assistance, or even a clear explanation. 

I never agreed to any monthly maintenance fee when I opened the account. This represents a retroactive and exploitative modification of terms, especially harmful to those in vulnerable financial situations. 

The option to reject this fee leads to account closure, which will negatively affect my credit utilization ratio, length of credit history, and overall score further exacerbating my financial recovery. 

In my opinion, this change is : Unfair and deceptive under UDAAP standards. 

Punitive in nature. 

Exploitative of data gathered during periods of active dispute. 

Despite their claims, Avant has never had a personal issue with my account specifically, and I have never given them reason to treat me as a risk warranting monthly penalties. The sudden addition of fees now ; when I am already financially vulnerable feels like a cruel and calculated move to exploit my situation rather than support a long-standing customer. It is incredibly disappointing and frankly predatory. 

Instead of being transparent and closing the account themselves ( as many creditors do when they feel a customer no longer meets their risk standards ), Avant is forcing the burden onto me to make it look as though I chose to close the account... likely to avoid regulatory scrutiny. This maneuver is manipulative, self-serving, and absolutely not in the spirit of consumer protection. Their actions clearly show they do not have the customers best interest at heart, and honestly, it raises the question : why would any consumer want to continue a financial relationship with a company that behaves this way?

Continuing to Report Inaccurate Data After Notification ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) ) Despite clear fraud reports, Experian continues to report these as valid, impacting my score and creditworthiness. 

When my information is being furnished or in your case parroted, you have obligations under the FCRA to ensure the accuracy of the information you furnish. As a rule, its illegal to report information that you know or believe is inaccurate. You have " reasonable cause to believe '' that information is inaccurate if you have knowledge, other than allegations from the consumer, that would lead a reasonable person to doubt the accuracy of the information. FCRA Section 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ). You may be exempt from this requirement if you give an address for consumers to report inaccurate information, but you can not, under any circumstances, report information the consumer has told you is inaccurate if it is, in fact, inaccurate. FCRA Section 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( C ) If you dont comply with the FCRA, you may be sued by the FTC , Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ), state governments, or in some cases, consumers. The FCRA provides for maximum penalties of {$4900.00} per violation in the case of lawsuits brought by the FTC. FCRA 616, 617, 621.

narrative:
I am filing a complaint against Midland Credit Management for violating the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) by knowingly reporting a collection account with fraudulent charges to the credit bureaus, after I notified them of the fraudulent activity and disputed the debt. 

On XX/XX/year>, I spoke by phone with a representative from Midland Credit Management and informed them that although I did open the original account, a number of charges reflected on the account were fraudulent and not authorized by me. I explained that I was a victim of identity theft or financial abuse, and that I was not responsible for the full balance they were attempting to collect. 

I recorded this phone call, which clearly shows that I disputed the account balance and alerted Midland that it contained fraudulent activity. Despite this, Midland Credit Management reported the collection account to the credit bureaus on XX/XX/year>, without properly investigating my dispute, and without marking the account as disputed, which is a violation of my consumer rights. 

Their conduct violates the following laws : FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 3 ) Furnishers must not report information they know or believe is inaccurate.

FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 2 ) Once a consumer disputes an account, the furnisher must investigate and correct or delete any inaccurate or unverifiable information.

FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) It is unlawful to furnish data to credit bureaus that is known to be inaccurate.

FDCPA 807 ( 8 ) Debt collectors must report a debt as disputed if the consumer has informed them of a dispute.

As a result of this failure to follow proper investigation procedures and knowingly reporting an account with fraudulent charges, my credit has been damaged. I am requesting that the CFPB investigate Midland Credit Management and : Require them to conduct a full and fair investigation, Mark the account as disputed with all credit bureaus, and Remove or adjust the inaccurate charges and balance accordingly.

I am prepared to submit a copy of the recorded call, a statement explaining the disputed charges, and any additional documentation to support my claim.

My personal information was compromised in a data breach involving XXXX. As a result, I have become a victim of identity theft. Actions Taken : I am formally disputing these accounts and requesting their immediate investigation and removal from my credit report. I am asserting my rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), which protects consumers from the reporting of inaccurate and fraudulent information.

Applicable FCRA Laws Supporting My Dispute : FCRA 611 ( 15 U.S. Code 1681i ) Procedure in case of disputed accuracy I have the right to dispute inaccurate or incomplete information on my credit report. The credit reporting agency is required to investigate the dispute within 30 days and remove or correct the information if it is found to be inaccurate, incomplete, or unverifiable.

FCRA 605B ( 15 U.S. Code 1681c-2 ) Block of information resulting from identity theft Upon providing proof of identity theft ( e.g., a police report or FTC Identity Theft Affidavit ), the consumer reporting agency must block the fraudulent information from appearing on the credit report within XXXX business days. 

FCRA 602 ( A ) Right to fair and accurate credit reporting The FCRA emphasizes that consumer reporting agencies must maintain accurate and fair credit files. Reporting fraudulent accounts caused by identity theft violates this standard.

FCRA 623 ( 15 U.S. Code 1681s-2 ) Responsibilities of furnishers of information The companies that supplied this false information to the credit bureaus ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. ) have a legal duty to investigate the accuracy of the data and must correct or delete it if it is found to be inaccurate or the result of identity theft.

issue: Attempts to collect debt not owed
narrative: The debt collector is reporting collection accounts to credit reporting agencies without establishing proper legal ownership or chain of title for the alleged debts. In the modern credit industry, original creditors routinely transfer and securitize their receivables through complex financial structures, often selling them to securitization trusts where the trust becomes the legal owner, not the debt collector. Despite these ownership changes, consumers are never notified of transfers, and debt collectors continue reporting and collecting on accounts they can not prove they legally own. Despite the mismatch between the account holder name and the intended beneficiary name, JPMorgan Chase Bank still credited the funds to the scammers account. The bank later confirmed that the account holder name did not match the listed beneficiary which is a clear violation of standard wire transfer verification practices and UCC 4A-207. 

I reported the fraud to JPMorgan Chase Bank, and they acknowledged the discrepancy. However, they did not reverse the transaction or issue a refund. I contacted JPMorgans call center and spoke to a representative named XXXX, who confirmed that if a mismatch occurred between the beneficiarys name and account number, the funds would not be credited and would be refunded to the sender within 14 days. The police conducted their own investigation and sent a formal letter to JPMorgan Chase requesting clarification. JPMorgan replied with a letter stating that they needed additional time to investigate and would respond. Since then, they have not followed up neither with the police department, my attorney, nor with me. 

I am currently in the United States on a temporary visit, which has allowed me to reopen this matter with the seriousness it deserves. equires furnishers to report only accurate, verifiable information and correct inaccuracies upon notice.

15 U.S. Code 1681i : Requires consumer reporting agencies to investigate disputes and delete unverifiable or inaccurate information within 30 days.

15 U.S. Code 1681c-2 : Provides for blocking information resulting from identity theft or fraudulent use of personal identifying information.

15 U.S. Code 45 ( FTC Act ) : Prohibits unfair or deceptive acts or practices, which includes the reporting of inaccurate consumer data.

sub_issue: Credit card company won't increase or decrease your credit limit
narrative:
On XX/XX/, Goldman Sachs Bank USA denied my Apple Card credit-limit increase ( CLI ). The adverse-action message states only : Your recent payments on Apple Card did not cover a significant portion of your monthly balance. It also lists my credit score as XXXX  XXXX Score XXXX : XXXX and says Goldman obtained my score from XXXX XXXX XXXX This was the full text of the notice. 

Why I believe this violates ECOA/Reg B ( 12 C.F.R. 1002.9 ) : 1. Required ECOA content is missing. Reg B requires every adverse-action notice to include the ECOA anti-discrimination statement and the name/address of the appropriate federal enforcement agency, in addition to the action taken and either the specific reasons or a notice of the right to request them. My notice includes the action and a reason, but it omits the ECOA rights statement and the enforcement-agency name/address. 
2. The specific reasons are not specific. Reg B requires reasons that are specific and accurately describe the principal factors considered. The phrase recent and significant portion is indeterminate and provides no time window or threshold. A compliant reason would state something like paid only the minimum in X of the last Y cycles or average payment <10 % of statement balance for Z months. As worded, I can not understand or remedy the issue. 
3. Potential omission of other principal reasons. The notice simultaneously discloses that a credit score was obtained/used ( XXXX  XXXX XXXX = XXXX ). If score-related factors ( e.g., utilization/delinquency ) were principal reasons, Reg B requires that none of the principal reasons be omitted. Listing only a payment-behavior line suggests other principal factors may have been excluded. 

Why I believe this also violates the FCRA ( 15 U.S.C. 1681m ( a ) and 1681g ( f ) ) : Because Goldman says it used my credit score in taking adverse action, the notice must also include : The CRAs name, address, and phone, a statement that the CRA did not make the decision, and my right to a free report and to dispute accuracy ( 1681m ( a ) ) ; and The credit-score range for that model and the key factors adversely affecting my score, in addition to score/model/date ( 1681g ( f ) ).

My notice includes only the score/model/date and the CRA namebut lacks the CRA contact/rights language, the score range, and the key factors.

BoFAs systems should have automatically flagged, held, and verified this transaction. I received no warning, no verification call, and no opportunity to stop it.

issue: Attempts to collect debt not owed
narrative:
I am filing this complaint because the company failed to properly validate a debt I disputed. Under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ), and related consumer protection statutes, a consumer has the right to request a full and verifiable validation of any alleged debt before it can be collected or reported.

I exercised this right and formally requested specific documentation to prove the validity and ownership of the alleged account. The company responded by sending only a generic bank statement. This does not meet the legal standard for debt validation, as it fails to prove the existence, ownership, and enforceability of the alleged debt. 

Specifically, the company failed to provide the following documents I demanded, which are necessary to establish legal standing and verification : Original signed contract Proof that I personally entered into a binding agreement with the original creditor. 

Full chain of title All assignments, transfers, and ownership records from the original creditor to the present entity. 

Proof of Holder in Due Course status As required under the Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ) Articles 3 and 9.

Transfer documents under 15 U.S.C. 1641 ( g ) ( TILA ) Showing legal transfer and notice of such transfer.

Pooling and Servicing Agreement identification If the alleged debt was securitized, the PSA and Schedule of Assets identifying the specific account. 

By failing to provide these documents, the company has not validated the alleged debt. A mere bank statement does not prove liability, ownership, or the legal right to collect. Therefore, the continued reporting or collection activity on this account constitutes a violation of my rights under the FDCPA and the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ).

issue: Attempts to collect debt not owed
narrative:
I received a letter dated XX/XX/year>, from Nelson & Kennard XXXX attempting to collect an alleged XXXX  XXXX XXXX charged-off account. The letter is on attorney letterhead listing numerous lawyers, but in the fine print they disclose : Nelson & Kennard, LLP is a debt collector. This communication raises several serious violations : 1. False or misleading representation ( 1692e FDCPA ) : The letter strongly implies attorney involvement and review, but no licensed attorney appears to have reviewed my account individually. Using attorney letterhead without actual legal involvement is deceptive and intimidating.

Listing numerous state bar licenses while functioning purely as a collection agency is a misrepresentation intended to pressure the consumer.

2. Failure to provide validation of debt ( 1692g FDCPA ) : The letter does not provide any proof of ownership, assignment, or contract. It references a XXXX  XXXX XXXX account that was already charged-off. 
No supporting documents were included with their initial communication, which is a violation.

3. Collecting without proof of standing : If Nelson & Kennard owns the account, they must disclose assignment/chain of title. If they do not, they are attempting to collect without proof they are the rightful creditor.

This is a direct violation of both the FDCPA and Californias Rosenthal Fair Debt Collection Practices Act.

4. Threat of credit reporting without validation : Their letter pressures me to pay or respond, but does not acknowledge that they can not legally report this to consumer reporting agencies without validation.

5. California Rosenthal Act violations : This firm is operating in California and is therefore subject to additional protections for consumers. Their letter engages in misleading intimidation tactics that are prohibited.

narrative:
I am filing this complaint regarding my recent application on XXXX XX/XX/XXXX for the Chase Freedom Unlimited credit card. Despite my strong financial qualifications, I was denied, and the reasons given reflect opaque internal policies that were not disclosed before applying. 

I am a veteran with 13 years of military service and hold a 100 % permanent and total XXXX rating. After leaving the military two years ago, I have worked hard to build my financial stability. My income has grown significantly. I now earn approximately quadruple what my annual income was during my military service. My credit scores are excellent : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. I maintain less than 5 % utilization on my existing {$87000.00} in credit lines. 

I applied for the Chase Freedom Unlimited card because of its 0 % introductory APR, intending to responsibly manage unplanned family expenses related to the recent passing of my father. To my surprise, I was denied, not due to my creditworthiness, but because of Chases 5/24 rule ( an internal policy that automatically denies applicants with 5+ new accounts in the past 24 months, regardless of financial strength ) and recent credit inquiries. The representative explicitly confirmed these were the reasons. 

My concerns are as follows : 1. Lack of Transparency : At no point during the application process was I warned that my application would be automatically denied due to this internal policy. Had I been aware, I would not have applied.

2. Hard Inquiry Penalty : The denial still resulted in a hard credit inquiry, which negatively impacts my credit score, despite Chase knowing in advance they would not approve the application due to this rigid policy.

3. Failure to Consider Full Profile : The bank did not provide a manual review option or allow reallocation of existing Chase credit lines ( I am already a Chase Sapphire Reserve cardholder in good standing ).

4. Punitive to Responsible Borrowers : I feel I am being punished for responsibly opening and managing credit cards as part of building my credit profile, despite maintaining extremely low utilization and excellent payment history. 
5. Disproportionate Impact on Veterans : As a XXXX veteran, I feel this rigid policy, coupled with the lack of transparency, unfairly limits my access to responsible credit management tools. 

I respectfully request that the CFPB review this matter to ensure : Chase provides clear disclosures upfront about internal policies ( like the 5/24 rule ) that automatically disqualify applicants, Consumers are not penalized with unnecessary hard inquiries when denials are predetermined by rigid criteria, Consideration is given for manual review when an applicant demonstrates strong financial standing and responsible credit use, especially in cases involving veterans managing hardship. 

This experience has left me frustrated and disadvantaged at a time when I most needed flexibility to manage my familys finances. I believe greater transparency and fairness in the process are warranted.

I relied in good faith on those assurances and suffered financial harm as a result. Had I been properly informed at the time of account opening, I would never have agreed to open these accounts. 
Instead of taking responsibility, PNC now suggests that I cancel my CD account after XX/XX/year>, without penalty, and receive only the first month of interest. I am submitting this complaint regarding U.S. Banks improper withdrawal of federally protected Title IV student aid funds from my savings account. 

On XX/XX/XXXX and XXXX ( 2025 ), I transferred {$3800.00} in tuition and housing funds derived from my Pell Grant and federal student loan disbursement into my U.S. Bank savings account. Days later, I was notified of a {$3700.00} withdrawal labeled travel. Believing this to be fraudulent, I immediately called to dispute the transaction. Instead of processing my claim, I was informed by U.S. Bank representatives that the bank had seized my funds to satisfy an outstanding balance on a business credit card account. 

This action is unlawful because the funds in question are Title IV federal student aid disbursements, which are subject to strict protections under the Higher Education Act ( 20 U.S.C. 1095a and related regulations ). These funds are provided for the exclusive purpose of covering educational expenses such as tuition, housing, and books, and banks are prohibited from offsetting, garnishing, or otherwise redirecting such funds to cover unrelated debts once disbursed. 
By seizing these funds, U.S. Bank : 1. Violated federal law that protects Title IV funds from setoff or garnishment.

2. Deprived me of the ability to pay for essential educational expenses, putting my housing and enrollment at risk.

3. Failed to provide transparency and due process, as the transaction was misleadingly labeled travel rather than disclosed as a setoff.

I am requesting that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau : Investigate U.S. Banks unlawful seizure of my Title IV funds, Require U.S. Bank to immediately return the full {$3700.00} to my account, and Ensure corrective action is taken so that student borrowers are not subjected to similar violations in the future. 

Students depend on these federal funds to pursue their education. Allowing banks to divert them for unrelated debts undermines both the intent of the law and the financial protections guaranteed to borrowers.

To whom it may concern 15 U.S.C. 1681b ( f ) Permissible purposes of consumer reports Credit inquiries must have a valid purpose ( e.g., your consent ).

Unauthorized inquiries are unlawful.

15 U.S.C. 1681c Requirements relating to information on consumer reports Restricts obsolete or inaccurate information from being reported.

15 U.S.C. 1681c-2 Blocking of information resulting from identity theft 15 U.S.C. 1681i Procedure in case of disputed accuracy Requires credit bureaus to investigate disputes within 30 days and delete unverifiable or inaccurate information. 

15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) Duties of furnishers of information Creditors can not knowingly report inaccurate or fraudulent information.

15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) Duties of furnishers after notice of dispute Once notified by a CRA, furnishers must investigate and correct/delete inaccurate info.

15 U.S.C. 1681a ( c ) Definition of consumer report Confirms that credit inquiries are part of a consumer report and covered under the Act.

15 U.S.C. 1681g Disclosures to consumers You have the right to request full disclosure of your credit file, including who made inquiries.

15 U.S.C. 1681j Charges for disclosures You are entitled to a free credit report annually and when you are a victim of identity theft.

15 U.S.C. 1681m Duties of users taking adverse actions If you are denied credit due to inaccurate info, the user must inform you and provide bureau details.

15 U.S.C. 1681n Civil liability for willful noncompliance You can sue for damages, attorneys fees, and punitive damages if bureaus/furnishers willfully fail to comply.

15 U.S.C. 1681o Civil liability for negligent noncompliance You can sue for damages if negligence leads to inaccurate reporting.

15 U.S.C. 1681p Jurisdiction of courts ; limitation of actions Gives you the right to bring action in federal or state court.

15 U.S.C. 1681q Obtaining information under false pretenses Prohibits unauthorized access or inquiries into your credit.

15 U.S.C. 1681s Administrative enforcement Gives the FTC, CFPB, and other agencies authority to enforce FCRA compliance.

The tradeline in question is being reported as both Bankruptcy and Deferred. This is inaccurate, misleading, and violates the Metro 2 Credit Reporting Resource Guide. 
I am currently enrolled in school, and my loan is in an approved deferment status. 
Under Metro 2 standards, an account can not simultaneously be coded as Bankruptcy ( Compliance Condition Code ) and Deferred ( Account Status ). These are mutually exclusive statuses. 
Reporting both together is contradictory and creates a false impression that my student loan has been legally discharged when in fact it is simply in deferment. 
This erroneous reporting is harming my credit profile and constitutes a violation of the FCRAs requirement for maximum possible accuracy. 
Requested Action : Immediately investigate and correct this reporting.

I respectfully disagree with their conclusion and maintain that the reported information is incomplete, misleading, and must be removed under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681i and 1681s-2. 

Grounds for Dispute : Inconsistent and Incomplete Recordkeeping Wells Fargo relies on statements from XXXX XXXX to justify late reporting. However, their records do not reflect the specific circumstances surrounding the alleged payment delays, including : Whether payment processing delays occurred between institutions. 

Whether payments were returned due to technical or institutional error. 

Whether grace periods, hardship accommodations, or internal posting errors contributed. 

Reporting such payments as late without including these relevant details renders the reporting incomplete and misleading, which is prohibited by FCRA 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ).

Failure to Consider Financial Hardship The alleged delinquencies occurred during a period of documented financial hardship. FCRA and CFPB guidance emphasize the duty to ensure reporting reflects fairness and accuracy. Wells Fargos rigid application of past due without acknowledgment of context unfairly penalizes me years later.

Obsolete and Disproportionate Impact These isolated XXXX incidents are now over six years old, with the account long since closed and paid in full. Continuing to report derogatory information at this stage is no longer serving any permissible purpose under FCRA 605 ( a ). Retaining such negative marks severely distorts my creditworthiness despite the accounts resolution.

Request for Reinvestigation Wells Fargo states the case is closed. However, under FCRA 1681i, a furnisher can not unilaterally close a dispute while new or clarifying evidence is presented. This letter and my prior submissions constitute additional evidence requiring reinvestigation.

Requested Resolution : Immediate deletion of the derogatory 30 days late reporting for XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX from my credit reports with all Consumer Reporting Agencies. 

Written confirmation to me and the CFPB that the deletion has been processed. 

I have exercised my rights under the FCRA in good faith. Should Wells Fargo fail to correct or remove this inaccurate and misleading reporting, I reserve the right to pursue further remedies, including regulatory escalation or civil action.

I also possess the original creditors sale notice showing {$1500.00} ( different amount ) and the collection timeline appears re-aged/inconsistent with the true history. 

XXXX  XXXX ( opened XX/XX/XXXX ) Status Paid in settlement. {$470.00} written off ( XX/XX/XXXX ) but Experians grid continues to post CO/charge-off months afterwards, which conflicts with a settled/closed status. 

XX/XX/XXXX I mailed Experian a written dispute under 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 1 ) identifying these items and requesting reinvestigation and deletion/correction.

XX/XX/XXXX Experian emailed me a Stall Response/Form Letter '' claiming my dispute did not appear to originate from me and refused to reinvestigate. 

XX/XX/XXXX Experian received my Final Demand Letter with documentation ( certified ). 

XX/XX/XXXX Experian sent an identical stall response, again refusing to investigate. 

Why this violates the FCRA : 1681i ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) Once Experian received my dispute, it was required to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation. Instead, Experian twice refused to investigate based on an incorrect third-party assertion, despite my prior identity verification call. 
1681i ( a ) ( 2 ) Experian must promptly notify the furnishers of the disputed information. Their stall letters indicate they did not transmit my dispute, depriving me of a reinvestigation by the furnishers.

1681i ( a ) ( 6 ) After reinvestigation, Experian must report results and, upon request, provide the description of the procedure used to determine accuracy, including the furnishers name, address, and telephone number ( 1681i ( a ) ( 6 ) ( B ) ( iii ) ). Because Experian refused to reinvestigate, I received none of this required information.

1681e ( b ) Experian must follow reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy. The contradictory charge-off/payment-grid data and the collection record without a disclosed DOFD show Experian is publishing information that is inaccurate/misleading on its face.

1681c ( obsolescence/DOFD ) Collections must be reported using the original creditor DOFD ; Experians XXXX tradeline fails to disclose and appears to use a later date, which risks re-aging.

I am submitting this complaint to dispute a false late payment reported by XXXX XXXX XXXX account number XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX on my credit report. This information is inaccurate and has negatively impacted my credit profile. 

Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), I have the right to dispute any information that is incomplete or inaccurate. Specifically : 15 U.S.C. 1681i requires credit reporting agencies ( CRAs ) to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation of disputed information within 30 days of receiving notice 1.

If the information can not be verified, it must be deleted from the credit report.

Additionally, 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) mandates that CRAs must follow reasonable procedures to ensure maximum possible accuracy of the information they report 1.

I have already contacted the credit bureau and the furnisher, XXXX XXXX XXXX, to dispute this late payment, but the issue remains unresolved. I am requesting the CFPB to : Investigate the reporting practices of XXXX XXXX XXXX  regarding this account. 
Ensure compliance with the FCRA and that the disputed late payment is either verified with supporting documentation or removed. 
Confirm that no further harm is done to my credit profile due to this inaccurate reporting. 

Thank you for your attention to this matter and for protecting consumers from inaccurate and harmful credit reporting practices.

Avante USA has continued to furnish this debt without proper verification.

Proof of identity and address as required for verification purposes.

When reviewing my Equifax credit report, I noticed that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( Account : XXXX ) is being reported with a late payment dated XX/XX/year>. What makes this reporting inaccurate is that the account is simultaneously listed as having a past due amount of {$0.00}. Yet Equifax continues to publish a derogatory late payment mark that directly contradicts the rest of the data being reported. 

This kind of conflicting information is not only misleading but unlawful under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, specifically 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), which requires consumer reporting agencies to ensure that information in consumer reports is accurate and not misleading. A late payment that is tied to a past due amount : {$0.00} is misleading because it suggests delinquency when in fact none existed.

The damage from this inaccuracy is not theoretical. Having a late payment notation on my file has caused real harm to my financial life. Late payments are among the most damaging pieces of information a credit bureau can report. Even a single misreported late payment can cause significant drops in credit scores, which in turn affect credit approvals, loan terms, and even housing opportunities. I have had to face awkward explanations with lenders who question why my report shows a delinquency on an account where the creditor itself reports no past due balance. The stress, wasted time, and reputational harm are real and ongoing.

Equifax has a duty under 15 U.S.C. 1681i to reinvestigate any disputed item and remove or correct it if it can not be verified with original creditor documentation. Unless Equifax can provide actual billing records from XXXX XXXX showing a legitimate past due balance at the time, this reporting is inaccurate and must be corrected. Anything short of that would be a violation of my rights under federal law.

narrative:
Follow up to case : XXXX Bank set off account without proper action. 

Under the Uniform Commercial Code ( XXXX XXXX ), banks XXXX exercise a right of setoff by applying funds in a customers deposit account toward debts owed to the bank. However, this right is limited by law and must be exercised in compliance with good faith and commercially reasonable practices. Key Principles : Authorization Requirement : A setoff may only be exercised if clearly authorized by the account agreement. Ambiguous or undisclosed terms are not sufficient to allow unilateral withdrawal of funds. Duty of XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX : Even where a contractual setoff clause exists, the bank must act in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner. Seizing funds without notice or while simultaneously failing to process agreed automatic payments does not meet this standard. XXXX of XXXX Obligations ( XXXX XXXX ) : A bank must honor properly payable items ( e.g., checks or authorized electronic transfers ) once they have been accepted for processing. Exercising setoff in a way that causes the dishonor of legitimate payments is inconsistent with the UCCs requirements. Application to XXXX XXXX XXXX : Lack of Informed Consent : I was never explicitly told that setoff would authorize Wells Fargo to withdraw funds from my account without my signature or contemporaneous authorization. Failure of XXXX XXXX : Wells Fargo failed to process my scheduled automatic payments ( an error on its part ), then used setoff to seize funds without notice, exacerbating financial harm. XXXX XXXX : XXXX XXXX setoff was applied before honoring my e-check to my attorney, resulting in a dishonored check. This contravenes XXXX XXXX, which restricts banks from prioritizing setoff over valid payment obligations. Lack of Notice : Reasonable notice is generally expected before setoff so that the customer can make alternative arrangements. Wells Fargo provided none. XXXX XXXX provides banks with a limited right of setoff, that right is constrained by principles of good faith, proper authorization, and fair dealing. XXXX XXXX actionsfailure to process auto-payments, unilateral XXXX of funds without warning, and dishonoring of other legitimate paymentsrepresent a misuse of setoff authority and a violation of these legal standards.

Earlier in the year Mr Cooper improperly denied my request for a loan assumption ( loan # XXXX ) based on the conclusion that because the property is not my primary residence it does not meet the requirements in XXXX XXXX loan servicing guide for transfers. In fact, XXXX XXXX loan servicing guide DOES have legal language that protects transfers like mine due to divorce and specific language in section 8406.1 sections c and d : " If the transferee requests to assume the Mortgage and/or the transferor requests to be released from liability, then the Servicer must determine the creditworthiness of the transferee in accordance with the requirements in Sections 8406.2 ( a ) and 8406.2 ( b ). '' The word " must '' is a mandate. It requires the servicer to proceed to a credit evaluation, not to issue a summary denial based on occupancy.

The servicer is denying based on the opening of the section 8406.1d part ii which mentions primary residence as a condition. The opening sentence is a general condition for when a servicer can't accelerate a loan. However, the final paragraph provides a specific, overriding instruction for a specific action : the request for a release of liability. 

For reference I was also able to successfully complete the release of liablility process for a second home, a non-primary residence with the loan servicer XXXX XXXX for loan # XXXX which is also a XXXX XXXX loan. This suggests Mr Cooper 's interpretation of the XXXX XXXX guide is in error. XXXX XXXX understood a request for release of liability understood the use of the word 'must ' in the regulatory guidelines and provided a process for release of liability.

I am writing to file a formal complaint against Barclays Bank Delaware regarding its handling of my fraud dispute ( Account ending in XXXX ).

Failure to Properly Investigate Simply concluding that the charges were made by me or someone with authority is inadequate without demonstrating how such a conclusion was reached. No details of the investigation, merchant records, or other supporting information were shared with me. 

Violation of Consumer Protections Under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ) and Regulation Z, issuers are required to conduct a reasonable investigation of disputed charges. I believe Barclays response fails to meet this standard, as they have not proven the legitimacy of the disputed transactions. 

As a consumer, I should not be held liable for fraudulent transactions unless the issuer can provide clear and convincing evidence that I authorized them. Barclays has not met this burden.

Unlawful Furnishing and Liability Continued reporting of unverified and inaccurate data violates 15 USC 1681s-2 ( b ) ( 2 ).

They also contradicted their own refund policy : I was told a POA had been filed ( which would limit me to a 25 % refund ) yet was offered a 50 % refund instead. These conflicting statements show the merchant did not follow its own terms.

Agents themselves admitted this inconsistency. I was given conflicting phone numbers, timelines, and explanations. One agent even declined to record my statements, saying someone will listen to the call later. Others spoke so quickly and vaguely that it became impossible to get clarity.

After escalation, I was told different case managers were assigned ( first XXXX, later XXXX ) but neither provided a decision or call-back within the stated 10 business days. 

Wells Fargo denied my dispute based on the merchants response, which contained contradictory claims that a Power of Attorney had been filed ( suggesting work was done ) and simultaneously that services could be withheld until full payment ( suggesting work was not done ). Both can not be true. Either the service was attempted and failed, or it was withheld entirely, which proves the service was not meaningfully rendered Because Wells Fargo denied the second dispute, I lost {$250.00}, even though the first claim for the same situation was refunded. This inconsistency has caused significant financial hardship ; Ive struggled to pay for groceries and basic expenses. 

I am asking the CFPB to review Wells Fargos handling of my dispute and require them to reinstate my {$250.00} credit. Wells Fargo failed to handle the dispute consistently or fairly, despite clear evidence of services not rendered.

Subject : Second Formal Dispute of Inaccurate Charge-Off Reporting World Finance Account # XXXX To Whom It May Concern, I am writing to follow up on my initial dispute regarding the inaccurate and misleading reporting of the World Finance account XXXX # XXXX ), which continues to appear on my credit reportsmost notably with Transunion. 
Despite my previous correspondence, the account continues to be reported as a charge-off on a monthly basis, which is both factually incorrect and in violation of federal credit reporting standards. As previously stated, a charge-off is a one-time event and not a status that should be reapplied each month.. 
This reporting practice is : Misleading to current and future creditors, Inflating the delinquency 's recency, and Causing undue harm to my credit profile. 
This continued reporting contradicts : The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) [ 15 U.S. Code 1681 et seq ], which mandates accurate reporting, The Metro 2 reporting format, which clearly states that a charge-off is a singular, final eventnot a recurring status, And guidance from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) regarding the prohibition of re-aging debts and the expectation of fair, consistent, and truthful reporting.

I am formally requesting the following : 1. Immediate correction of the reporting to reflect a single, accurate charge-off date.

2. If this can not be done in full compliance with the FCRA and Metro 2 standards, then I request the complete deletion of this account from all consumer reporting agencies.

3. A written response indicating the outcome of your re-investigation, as required under the FCRA.

Im also requesting the following information : 1. The method of verification used to validate this charge-off account.

2. The name and contact information of the person or entity you spoke to during the verification process.

3. The date and time when this verification occurred.

4. All supporting documentation provided to substantiate the accuracy of this charge-off.

Furthermore, after this letter, if the problem is not corrected I will be contacting my Geogia States Attorney Office as well as filing legal complaints about these unlawful reporting practices with proof of tracking and evidence of correspondence of you violating Metro-2 Reporting Format and 15 U.S. Code 1681 et seq.

Please respond within 10 days of receipt of this letter. Again, I am retaining records of all correspondence for future reference and potential legal action if this matter is not resolved in compliance with federal law.

Thank you for your immediate attention to this matter. Please consider this letter a formal reiteration of my dispute under the FCRA.

sub_product: General-purpose credit card or charge card
narrative:
To the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am writing to file a formal complaint and raise serious concerns about a practice I have experienced with credit card issuers. On two separate occasions in the last year, I was laid off from my job. In both instances, within weeks of my employment ending, my credit card providers prompted me to update my income.

This pattern suggests that issuers are receiving timely, non-public information about my employment status, likely through third-party data aggregators or payroll data services, and are using it to proactively re-evaluate my account status. While I understand the need for lenders to manage risk and comply with the " ability to pay '' provisions of the CARD Act, the timing and method of these inquiries feel predatory and punitive. 
This practice targets consumers at a moment of acute financial vulnerability. An unexpected income verification prompt immediately after a job loss causes significant distress and creates fear that a primary financial tool could be restricted or closed when it is needed most. It raises the following questions that I urge the Bureau to investigate : Data Sourcing and Transparency : What specific data sources are credit card issuers using to receive near-real-time updates on a consumer 's employment status? Is the use of this data for proactive account management adequately disclosed to consumers? 
Unfair Practices ( UDAAP ) : Does this practice constitute an Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Act or Practice ( UDAAP )? Targeting individuals immediately after a job loss could be interpreted as taking unreasonable advantage of their situation and the lack of public knowledge about these data-sharing practices.

Spirit of the Law : Does this proactive, data-driven review align with the consumer-protection spirit of the CARD Act, or is it a punitive application of the rule that harms rather than helps consumers in precarious financial situations? 
This practice feels like a systemic overreach that can cause significant harm to consumers who have just lost their primary source of income. I request that the CFPB investigate the prevalence of this industry practice and assess its legality and fairness under current consumer protection laws. 
Thank you for your attention to this critical matter. 
Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

This complaint serves as my fifth and follow-up regarding inaccurate and unauthorized information that continues to appear across my credit reports with the three major credit bureaus. Despite multiple prior disputes and supporting evidence, the same unverified and misleading information remains. This continued reporting violates several key sections of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), including my rights under FCRA 611 ( a ) 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ), which requires credit bureaus to promptly delete or correct inaccurate information after a dispute, and FCRA 607 ( b ) 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), which mandates maximum possible accuracy in all consumer reports.

Please be advised that this is not a request for correction. I am demanding permanent deletion of the following account and inquiry, as neither have been lawfully verified or substantiated with proper documentation as required under FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ), which prohibits furnishers from providing information known to be inaccurate. 
Charged-Off Account in Dispute XXXX Account No XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  Balance Owed : {$0.00} This account continues to appear as a charge-off while reporting a zero-dollar balance. This is factually inconsistent and misleading, as a charge-off indicates an unpaid debt, yet the balance shows nothing owed. The reporting of this account in such a manner violates FCRA 607 ( b ), which requires all information reported to consumer reporting agencies to be complete and accurate.

Additionally, under FCRA 611 ( a ), credit reporting agencies must conduct a proper reinvestigation and delete any item that can not be verified within the legally required timeframe. Since no verifiable documentation or creditor validation has been produced in response to prior disputes, this tradeline must now be permanently deleted. Continuing to report this account also violates FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ), which explicitly forbids furnishers from reporting data they know or have reason to believe is inaccurate. 
Unauthorized Inquiry in Dispute XXXX XXXX  Date of Inquiry : XX/XX/year> This inquiry was made without my consent or authorization, and there is no permissible purpose for it under the law. Under FCRA 604 ( a ) 15 U.S.C. 1681b ( a ), a consumer report may only be accessed for specific, legitimate purposes, such as an approved credit application. Furthermore, FCRA 604 ( f ) 15 U.S.C. 1681b ( f ) prohibits any person from obtaining a consumer report without a permissible purpose. Obtaining my report without my consent constitutes unauthorized access, an
d under FCRA 619 15 U.S.C. 1681q, it is unlawful to obtain consumer information under false pretenses. Because this inquiry can not be verified or justified, it also falls under FCRA 605B 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2, which provides for the blocking and removal of information resulting from unauthorized or fraudulent use.

narrative:
On XX/XX/year>, I sent dispute letters to all three major credit bureaus ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, as well as to the headquarters of the dealership that purchased my leased vehicle. In my dispute, I explained that the dealership failed to remit payment for the vehicle buyout for approximately two ( 2 ) months after the date of sale, which falsely created the appearance of a 60-day delinquency on my credit report. This delinquency was not caused by me, as the dealership took possession of the vehicle and assumed responsibility for payment as part of the buyout process. 

I provided each party with : Proof of the date I sold/transferred the vehicle to the dealership Documentation from the dealership itself acknowledging when they finally submitted payment two months later ( which I had to personally force by visiting the dealership in person ) Highlighted discrepancies showing the gap between the sale date and their delayed payment submission, which caused the false derogatory reporting Despite being given clear documentation proving that the late payment was due solely to the dealerships delay and not my failure to pay, the credit bureaus responded stating they had verified and updated the account as accurate. The dealership headquarters likewise responded that the records were valid, ignoring the delayed remittance and the resulting wrongful delinquency reporting. 

There is no valid legal or contractual basis for me to be held responsible or reported late for payments after the dealership took control of the vehicle and delayed sending payment for two months. Their failure to remit timely payment has wrongly impacted my credit standing.

I am requesting : A full reinvestigation, Deletion or correction of the inaccurate delinquency reporting, Disclosure of their method of verification under FCRA 611, including who verified this information and what documentation was used.

The ongoing misreporting is causing me financial harm, emotional distress, and negative impact on my ability to obtain favorable credit terms. I provided documented proof that has been disregarded, and I believe the credit bureaus and dealer have failed to conduct a reasonable investigation as required under the Fair Credit Reporting Act. 

I am seeking the CFPBs assistance in compelling the credit bureaus and the dealership to properly investigate and correct this derogatory information that I did not cause.

narrative: I am filing this formal complaint against XXXX XXXX for unlawful reporting of a negative item on my credit file in violation of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA, 15 U.S.C. 1692 et seq. ) and the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA, 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq. ). This collection account is currently preventing me from securing a home for my family. The debt collector has : Failed to Provide Written Notice Under FDCPA 809 ( a ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( a ) ), a debt collector must provide written notice of the debt within five ( 5 ) days of the initial communication, including the amount of the debt and my right to dispute. I never received such notice. This omission is a direct violation of the FDCPA. Failure to Validate the Debt Case law has established that merely placing a tradeline on a consumers credit report without proper validation constitutes deceptive collection activity. In XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX. XXXX XXXX. 2001 ), the court ruled that reporting a debt to a credit bureau without first validating it violates the FDCPA. Lack of Authorization / Permissible Purpose Under FCRA 604 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681b ), a consumer reporting agency may only furnish a credit report if there is a permissible purpose initiated by the consumer. I never authorized this debt collector to access or furnish information about me. Absent my consent or a legitimate business purpose, their reporting is unlawful. Identity Theft & Blocking Rights Under FCRA 605B ( 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2 ), I have the right to demand a block of information resulting from alleged identity theft. Since I never authorized or entered into any agreement with this collector, their tradeline qualifies as unauthorized and must be blocked. Deceptive and Abusive Collection Tactics The CFPB and FTC have identified debt parking ( placing debts on consumer credit reports without notice ) as an unlawful and abusive practice. This is exactly what has occurred in my case.

At that time I also recieved a demand letter and I called again in late XXXX, then on or around XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/year>, and was repeatedly told that no decision had been made and that my file was still under review and in underwriting. On XX/XX/year>, I was told again that no decision had been issued, and that if the hardship request were denied, the loan would go directly into foreclosure next week ( this week ). 

Because of these delays and the instructions to stop payments, I listed the property for sale to try to prevent foreclosure. While the hardship was still being reviewed, M & T ( or its vendor ) falsely classified the property as abandoned, even though utilities were active, the home was maintained, and it was listed for sale. I contacted the property-preservation vendor several times in XX/XX/year> to correct this misinformation. 

On or around XX/XX/year>, I received a letter attempting to modify mortgage-insurance coverage without my consent, apparently based on the false abandonment claim. M & Ts actions have caused financial losses, including late fees, inspection charges, foreclosure costs, and harm to credit. 

These actions appear to violate : 12 C.F.R. 1024.41 ( dual tracking ) moving toward foreclosure while a loss-mitigation application is pending ; 12 C.F.R. 1024.35 ( failure to provide accurate information ) ; and 12 U.S.C. 2605 ( f ) creating borrower harm through mismanagement of servicing obligations. 

Requested resolution : Halt all foreclosure activity while the hardship is properly reviewed. 

Correct the false abandonment designation and withdraw any insurance changes. 

Provide a complete loss-mitigation and servicing record as required by RESPA. 

Reverse improper fees and charges and correct credit reporting. 

Provide damages for losses and pattern-of-practice violations.

narrative:
I am disputing the accuracy, completeness, and legality of the reporting of a negative JPMCB AUTO FINANCE account that is being reported beyond the allowable 7-year limit, contains incomplete payment history, and has been illegally re-aged by the data furnisher and/or credit reporting agency by providing an incorrect Date of First Delinquency ( DOFD ). 

Upon reviewing multiple credit reports from previous years, I confirmed that the original DOFD for this account was reported as XX/XX/XXXX. However, recent credit reports now show the earliest delinquency as XX/XX/XXXX, omitting the delinquency months of XXXX, XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX. This change effectively re-ages the account, extending its reporting period beyond what is legally permitted. 

The Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) explicitly limits the amount of time a negative account may appear on a consumer credit report. Under FCRA 605 ( a ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681c ( a ) ), adverse information such as late payments, charge-offs, or collections may not be reported beyond seven ( 7 ) years from the Date of First Delinquency that led to the accounts default. The DOFD establishes the start of this 7-year period. 

In addition, under FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 5 ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 5 ) ), furnishers of informationsuch as the creditor or lenderare required to accurately report the Date of First Delinquency to credit reporting agencies. This section prohibits a furnisher from altering or re-aging the DOFD to make a derogatory account appear newer or to allow it to remain on a consumers report longer than the law allows. 

By failing to report the full payment history and by modifying or omitting the original delinquency dates, the furnisher and/or credit bureau are in violation of FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) as well, which prohibits reporting information that is known or should reasonably be known to be inaccurate. 

These actions have the effect of misleading future creditors and unfairly harming my creditworthiness by allowing an obsolete and inaccurately dated negative account to continue reporting. Each inaccurate or omitted month ( XXXX, XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX ) represents an independent instance of noncompliance with the FCRA. 

Under FCRA 616 and 617 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681n and 1681o ), consumers are entitled to actual damages, statutory damages ( up to {$1000.00} per violation ), and, in cases of willful noncompliance, punitive damages, as well as costs and attorneys fees. 

For these reasons, I am requesting a full investigation into this accounts reporting history. Specifically, I request that the credit reporting agency and furnisher : Restore the original Date of First Delinquency ( XX/XX/XXXX ) as documented in prior credit reports ; Delete the account entirely from my credit file, as the lawful 7-year reporting period has expired based on the true DOFD ; Provide a written statement of the results of the reinvestigation within the 30-day period required under FCRA 611 ( a ) ; and Send me an updated copy of my credit report showing the corrected or deleted information. 

Failure to correct this inaccurate and obsolete reporting constitutes continued noncompliance with federal law and may result in further action or complaints to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) and/or the Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ). 

This dispute is being made in good faith and is supported by documentation, including copies of prior credit reports showing the original DOFD ( XX/XX/XXXX ) and the most recent version showing the incorrect XXXX ( XX/XX/XXXX ). 
Please investigate this matter promptly and ensure compliance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act.

I am filing this complaint about RAS LaVrar LLC, a law firm that is acting as XXXX XXXX counsel in an unconscionable consumer debt collection lawsuit against me. RAS LaVrar LLC is a debt collector under 15 U S C section 1692a 6 because it regularly collects consumer debts through litigation. The Supreme Court has held that attorneys who regularly engage in debt collection activity through lawsuits are covered debt collectors. See Heintz v Jenkins 514 U S 291 1995.

This alleged debt is the direct result of identity theft and is not my account. Before the hearing or trial date I sent a detailed written dispute and debt validation request to the plaintiff and to RAS LaVrar LLC. I clearly stated in writing that the account is the result of identity theft, that I did not open or authorize this account, and that any charges are not mine. I provided supporting documentation showing that my identification was compromised and that this account is fraudulent. 

I specifically asked them to treat the account as blocked for identity theft or, at a minimum, to validate the debt by providing documents that actually tie me personally to the account before continuing any collection activity or litigation. In other words, once they had my identity theft reports, the burden was on them to investigate and either prove it is my debt or stop collecting. 

Despite this, on XX/XX/XXXX the attorney from RAS LaVrar LLC appeared in court and openly admitted to the judge that they were not prepared. The attorney stated that they had not reviewed my identity theft materials and had not reviewed my written validation request. They did not have any documents with them to prove that I owed this debt. Instead of being ready to proceed or dismiss, they asked the court for a ninety day continuance so they could go back and review the file and my fraud materials.

This means RAS LaVrar LLC pushed an identity theft victim into a court proceeding without first reviewing the fraud reports that were already in their possession and without having any competent proof that I owed the debt. I had to prepare for court, take time to appear, and endure continuing stress and collection pressure while they freely admitted that they had not even looked at my identity theft evidence.

Their own court filings also carry the disclaimer in bold capital letters THIS IS AN ATTEMPT TO COLLECT A DEBT AND ANY INFORMATION OBTAINED WILL BE USED FOR THAT PURPOSE. THIS COMMUNICATION IS FROM A DEBT COLLECTOR. XXXX By placing this language on their pleadings, RAS LaVrar LLC is expressly acknowledging that its litigation activity is a communication in connection with the collection of a debt and that it is acting as a debt collector under the FDCPA. Yet at the same time, they ignored my identity theft dispute, failed to conduct a meaningful investigation, and advanced the lawsuit to a court date without the basic proof needed to show that I am the debtor.

In my view this conduct is abusive and deceptive under 15 U S C section 1692e and unfair under section 1692f. A law firm can not label its pleadings as a debt collection communication, admit in open court that it has not reviewed an identity theft victims documents or validation request, and still continue to use the lawsuit as a pressure tool against an ID Theft Victim.

narrative:

The transaction was not a point-of-sale swipe/tap/insert at any physical terminal ; it was an automated verification event associated with a hiring workflow. Treating this as a consumer-initiated, card-present denial is inaccurate and misleading, and it has had material adverse effects on my employment prospects and livelihood hour after hour as the error persists without meaningful review.

I notified Credit Karma through its dispute channels that the {$12.00} item was mischaracterized, not a consumer retail attempt, and that its labeling and status were harming my employment screening outcomes, yet Credit Karma has not corrected the record or provided evidence-based substantiation for the current reporting. The platform advertises a Direct Dispute workflow with TransUnion and guidance for handling errors, but the response I received did not address the substance ( bot-driven auth, no physical terminal, employment context ) and did not remediate the inaccurate characterization. This failure to reasonably investigate and correct inaccurate data violates basic credit-report dispute expectations and exacerbates ongoing damages tied to job eligibility and automated employment systems.

The inaccurate presentation suggests a consumer-initiated transaction at a physical reader was declined, which is not true. This creates the false impression of attempted misuse, insufficient funds behavior, or fraud flags connected to my identityan impression that can propagate through third-party screeners or internal risk models used by employers or gig platforms. The result is lost earning opportunities and reputational harm. The systems refusal to align the data with the actual event type ( an automated verification ping associated with hiring ) is unreasonable and misleading. 



I followed the standard steps : reviewed the item in XXXX XXXX, attempted to use their guided dispute pathway tied to TransUnion, and supplied clarifications showing the event was not a consumer retail interaction. XXXX XXXX public materials state consumers can dispute errors, and that erroneous information can be removed via Direct Dispute, but the company has not corrected the misclassification nor provided any documentation validating the denied at a physical reader narrative. I need a proper reinvestigation with attention to the event type, channel ( card-not-present vs. present ), and purpose ( employment verification ), along with removal or accurate reclassification of the erroneous entry. 



This continuing inaccuracy is time-sensitive because hiring systems often re-check or cache risk and identity signals ; the longer the mislabeling persists, the more opportunities are lost. The amount is {$12.00}, but the harm is not the amountits the misleading context of a supposed in-person denial and the failure to heed my dispute explaining the employment verification nature of the event. I am requesting the Bureaus assistance to prompt Credit Karma ( and any furnishing/reporting partners involved ) to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation, correct or delete the inaccurate characterization, and provide me with written confirmation of the changes

This letter also serves as a renewed formal request for full validation and a demand that this debt be deleted from all credit reporting agencies immediately.

FDCPA Violations ( 15 U.S.C. 1692 et seq. ) Under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), particularly 809 ( 15 U.S.C. 1692g ), a consumer has the right to request validation of any alleged debt. Upon receiving such a request, the debt collector must cease all collection efforts until proper validation is provided.

To date, Hunter Warfield has failed to provide the following required documents : The original signed agreement or lease showing I owe this debt.

The itemized statement or ledger showing how the balance was calculated.

The full account assignment or chain of title showing legal ownership and the right to collect.

By continuing to report and/or attempt to collect on an invalidated debt, Hunter Warfield is in violation of FDCPA 807 and 808 ( 15 U.S.C. 1692e1692f ), which prohibit false, deceptive, and unfair collection practices, including the reporting of unverified information to credit bureaus.

2. Regulation F ( 12 C.F.R. Part 1006 ) CFPB Implementation of the FDCPA Per Regulation F, issued by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( effective XX/XX/year> ), debt XXXX must not : Continue collection communications without first providing a complete validation notice ( 1006.34 ).

Report a debt to a credit bureau prior to providing the required validation notice ( 1006.30 ( a ) ).

Hunter Warfields ongoing communication and credit reporting activity without proper validation is a direct violation of these provisions.

3. Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq. ) Under the FCRA, data furnishers ( including debt collectors ) are required to report only accurate, validated and verifiable information to credit bureaus.

1681s-2 ( a ) prohibits the reporting of information known or reasonably should be known to be inaccurate.

1681i ( a ) requires credit reporting agencies to reinvestigate disputed information within 30 days.

Because Hunter Warfield has not provided verification or validation, any continued reporting of this debt to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXs inaccurate and unlawful. Therefore, I am demanding immediate deletion of this tradeline. 
XXXX. Uniform Commercial Code ( XXXX ) XXXX ( b ) ( XXXX ) and XXXX Under the UCC, the party XXXX a right to payment must produce the original instrument of indebtedness or an authenticated record evidencing the obligation.

narrative:
Company : Capital One Bank ( USA ), N.A. 
Product : Credit Card Account Type : Secured Credit Card ( XXXX XXXX  ) Account ending in : XXXX What happened : On XX/XX/2025, Capital One closed my secured XXXX credit card account and provided the explanation that the closure was due to activity inconsistent with typical customer account usage. This statement is vague and does not explain what specific activity allegedly prompted the action. 

I have not engaged in fraud, abuse, unauthorized use, or any conduct that would violate the cardholder agreement. I have maintained timely payments and used the account responsibly. I have requested clarification and reconsideration, but Capital One has not provided a specific reason as required by law. 

This constitutes an adverse action. Under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ), creditors are required to provide a specific, detailed reason for adverse action notices : 15 U.S.C. 1691 ( d ) ( 2 ) requires creditors to provide a statement of specific reasons for adverse action.

15 U.S.C. 1691 ( d ) ( 3 ) prohibits creditors from giving vague or generic explanations.

Regulation B ( 12 C.F.R. 1002.9 ( a ) ( 2 ) ) further requires that adverse action notices be clear and specific enough to allow the consumer to understand the basis of the decision. 

The explanation provided activity inconsistent with typical customer use is not specific and does not satisfy these requirements because it does not identify what behavior or transaction triggered the closure. 

Additionally, I am concerned that Capital One may report the closure to the credit bureaus inaccurately. The Fair Credit Reporting Act requires that any information furnished to credit reporting agencies must be accurate and not misleading : 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ).

What I am requesting : 1. A specific written explanation of the exact reason ( s ) the account was closed, as required under ECOA and Regulation B.

2. A review and reconsideration of the closure decision.

3. Assurance that no inaccurate or derogatory information regarding this closure will be furnished to any consumer reporting agency, consistent with FCRA accuracy requirements. 

I am requesting the CFPBs assistance in obtaining a lawful and transparent explanation and ensuring that my credit report is not harmed due to a non-specific or automated closure. 

Thank you.

narrative:
This is a supplemental complaint related to the previous complain ID XXXXI am submitting this formal rebuttal regarding my Bank of America fraud claim ( Claim # XXXX ). The bank issued two denial letters that are nearly identical, both failing to address my submitted evidence and lacking any substantive investigation in violation of the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA, 15 U.S.C. 1693 et seq. ) and Regulation E ( 12 CFR 1005 ).

1. Failure to Conduct a Reasonable Investigation Both denial letters contain only generic statements claiming the transaction was completed using a device consistent with previous valid account activity. No technical evidencesuch as IP address, device ID, or geolocation datawas provided. Under Regulation E ( 1005.11 ( b ) ( 1 ) ), a financial institution must conduct a reasonable investigation and provide a written explanation of findings. Copy-pasted conclusions do not meet this standard.

2. Ignored Evidence of SIM Swap Fraud I provided clear documentation proving my XXXX XXXX phone number was fraudulently ported to another SIM card before the transaction occurred. The authentication code was intercepted by criminals, not by me. Thus, the claim that the transaction was authorized via a valid phone number is false. 

3. Invalid Authentication and EFTA Protection Under EFTA 1693g ( a ) and CFPB Official Interpretation 1005.2 ( m ) -2, a transaction is unauthorized if access credentials were obtained through fraud ( such as a SIM swap ). SMS-based authentication does not constitute valid authorization when the device is compromised. 

4. Failure to Detect Red-Flag Activity Prior to the {$8000.00} wire on XXXX XXXX XXXX ( executed at XXXXXXXX XXXX  ), the fraudster performed multiple suspicious actions : password reset, adding a new wire recipient, enabling Apple Pay, and repeatedly accessing my account. These were obvious indicators of account takeover that Bank of America failed to act upon, violating the FTC Red Flags Rule ( 16 CFR 681.2 ).

5. Delayed Response and Customer Harm Around XXXXXXXX XXXX, within XXXX minutes of the transaction, I began calling Bank of America to report the incident. I was repeatedly placed on hold and transferred between departments. This delay prevented timely freezing of my account, directly increasing the loss. A customer should not bear financial responsibility for the banks inefficient response system. 

6. Lack of Accountability Despite submitting police and FTC reports, I have never been assigned a dedicated representative to handle my case. This lack of direct contact further hindered communication and resolution.

The investigation by Bank of America appears cursory and incomplete. Both denial letters are nearly identical and fail to address the evidence I submitted. I respectfully request that the CFPB require Bank of America to reopen the case, conduct a full forensic review ( including IP, device, and geolocation data ), and reimburse the {$8000.00} in compliance with EFTA 1693f and Regulation E 1005.11.
