I am disputing the derogatory account being reported by I C System because the information they are furnishing appears to be inaccurate, unverified, and not supported by any original documentation. When reviewing my credit reports, I noticed that I C System is reporting a collection account with a past-due balance, but none of the information has been validated or substantiated. 

I submitted disputes with the credit reporting agencies and specifically requested that I C System provide documentation verifying the account. I asked for the original creditor agreement, itemized billing statements, proof of ownership, chain of assignment, and the records used to calculate the reported balance. Instead of providing any of these documents, the credit bureaus responded with generic statements claiming the account was verified, but no supporting documentation was supplied, and I C System did not send me any validation records. 

I C System failed to provide original documentation proving the debt is valid or that they have the legal right to report it. They also did not provide a breakdown of the alleged balance, any billing history, or proof showing how the amount owed was determined. Without these documents, the accuracy and legitimacy of the reporting can not be confirmed. 

Additionally, the information I C System furnished appears inconsistently across different credit bureaus. There are discrepancies in dates, balance amounts, and status codes, which indicates the account was not properly verified before being reported. If each bureau shows different details for the same I C System account, the information can not be considered accurate or reliable. 

The account also was not marked as disputed, despite my formal disputes being submitted. Furnishers are required to add this notation when an account is under dispute, and failing to do so misleads lenders reviewing the file. 

Because I C System did not provide validation, is reporting inconsistent and inaccurate data, and has not demonstrated the accuracy of the derogatory information they furnished, I am requesting a full reinvestigation using original documentation. If I C System can not verify the account with proper evidence, the derogatory reporting should be removed from my credit file.

1. Summary of the Fraud I issued Check # XXXX payable to XXXX Treasury as an IRS tax payment. 
The check amount was {$2800.00}.

Only then did I discover the check had been altered to a different payee after I wrote it. 
The check I intended to pay to the XXXXXXXX XXXX  was criminally altered after issuance, and US Bank paid the altered item. 
2. US Bank Denied My Claim Improperly US Bank denied my reimbursement claim citing customer duty to examine statements within XXXX days. 
This denial is improper and contradicts the UCC, banking regulations, and reasonable consumer standards.

3. The check was materially altered therefore not properly payable ( UCC 4-401 and 3-407 ) Changing the payee name is a material alteration under UCC 3-407.

A bank may not charge a customers account for a materially altered check, because such an item is not properly payable under UCC 4-401.

US Bank charged my account for a check that was not the check I issued.

4. US Bank can not use the XXXX rule ( UCC 4-406 ) if the bank failed ordinary care Even if a customer delays reporting an issue, UCC 4-406 ( e ) ( f ) clearly states : A customer is NOT precluded from asserting an alteration If the bank failed to exercise ordinary care Or if the banks failure substantially contributed to the loss US Bank failed to detect an obvious alteration, despite having imaging systems and fraud-detection duties.

5. US Bank does NOT display the payee name unless the customer clicks deeper into each individual check image This is critical.

US Banks online system displays only : - check number - amount - posting date The payee name is NOT shown in the statement or transaction list. 
A customer must click and open the check image manually to see the payee something the UCC does NOT require, and something no reasonable customer is expected to do absent suspicion.

I verified the : check number ( matched ) check amount ( matched ) There was no visible discrepancy.

It was not reasonably possible for me to detect the alteration based on the information US Bank provided.

Expecting customers to click open every check image to discover what U.S. Bank itself failed to detect is unreasonable and contradicts the UCCs allocation of responsibility.

6. US Bank is improperly shifting liability for a criminal act onto the customer US Bank : Paid a materially altered check Failed to detect the alteration Provided no warning or system to help customers detect payee fraud Then denied my claim based on a technicality that does not apply to altered items This contradicts : UCC 3-407 UCC 4-401 UCC 4-406 ( e ) ( f ) OCC expectations for fraud handling General consumer protection principles

narrative:
I am requesting a full review and reclassification because my dispute was mishandled from the beginning, and the outcome has left me completely unprotected as a consumer. 

The order was placed with XXXX XXXX XXXX, a UK-based company. I was on their website only trying to view my total when the checkout screen auto-redirected through XXXX and processed the order before I intended to authorize it. 

On my first call to Wells Fargo, I specifically stated : I recognized the merchant I had ordered from them before I had my card in my possession I never suggested fraud, stolen card, or unknown merchant. When the representative asked if the charge was unauthorized, I said yes meaning I did not intend to place the order at that moment, not that someone else used my card. That misunderstanding caused my dispute to be coded incorrectly. 

When the items arrived, I called Wells Fargo again and openly stated I had received them. I was transparent about possession. 

Communication with XXXX XXXX XXXX was almost nonexistent. They have no U.S. phone number and respond extremely slowly to emails. I had minimal communication with them, which is why I sought help from Wells Fargo in the first place. 

A Wells Fargo representative instructed me to return the merchandise. I followed those instructions. The items were delivered back to the merchant on XX/XX/year>, under tracking XXXX. 

Despite having their merchandise back since XX/XX/XXXX, the merchant never refunded me. They responded to XXXX XXXX investigation in XXXX but did not disclose that they were already in possession of the returned items. This omission materially affected my dispute. 

XXXX The Label did not contact me at all until yesterday, after both the dispute and the appeal were closed in their favor. In that message, they falsely claimed Wells Fargo was responsible for issuing the refund. A Wells Fargo supervisor confirmed this was not true, and she also stated she did not know why the merchant would tell me that.

I have now sent over 15 emails to the merchant including all documentation, tracking proof, dates, screenshots, delivery confirmation, and explanation. They are now completely ignoring me. 

As it stands, the merchant has : their merchandise back since XX/XX/XXXX my payment of {$150.00} and they are refusing to respond or issue a refund While I am left with nothing. No product, no refund, no help, and no accountability from either party. 

This situation has left me feeling completely defeated as a consumer. I did everything correctly : I reported the issue, I clarified the misunderstanding, I followed Wells Fargos instructions, and I returned the items. Yet the merchant has kept both their merchandise and my money. 

I strongly believe this situation is unfair, improper, and potentially illegal. A merchant should not be allowed to keep both the product and the payment, especially when they misled the bank by not disclosing the return. 

The denial of my dispute and appeal happened solely because the claim was misclassified as unauthorized, and the dispute team told me they can not override that category. This prevented the bank from considering : the unintentional checkout that I recognized the merchant that I possessed my card that I acknowledged receiving the items that Wells Fargo instructed me to return the items proof of the return the merchants failure to refund me and the merchant ignoring me after receiving the return This is clearly a merchant/return dispute, and I am requesting a full reclassification and proper evaluation by the Executive Office so that the actual evidence can be reviewed and the situation can be resolved fairly.

narrative:
XXXX XXXX is inaccurately reporting multiple 180 days past due delinquencies on my HELOC ( ending XXXX ), including for months that were covered by a mutually agreed forbearance period. These XXXX delinquencies do not reflect my actual payment history and contradict federal credit reporting rules. 

We entered a forbearance in XXXX. During a forbearance, payments are deferred by agreement. Under the CARES Act XXXX ( amending FCRA XXXX ( a ) ( XXXX ) ( F ) ), any account that was current at the start of a forbearance must be reported as current for the entire duration of the forbearance, and the lender XXXX not report the forbearance months as delinquent. 

Despite this, XXXX XXXX is treating the entire forbearance period as if it were delinquent and is lumping those months into a XXXX delinquency after the forbearance ended. This is not allowed. A missed payment after the forbearance ends XXXX start a new delinquency, but delinquency can not be backdated into the forbearance period. 

In addition, the reporting is inconsistent across all three credit bureaus : TransUnion shows 180 days late in XX/XX/XXXX Experian shows 180 days late in XX/XX/XXXX Equifax shows 180 days late in XX/XX/XXXX The account then shows as current shortly after. It is not mathematically or procedurally possible for an account to be 180 days delinquent in several different months and then immediately current. This clearly indicates incorrect reporting. 

I spoke with a representative ( XXXX XXXX ), who stated that because I did not make a payment immediately when the forbearance ended, the bank considered the entire forbearance period delinquent and aged it into a XXXX late. This is not how delinquency aging works under the FCRA or XXXX guidelines. Delinquency must be aged based on consecutive missed cycles after the accommodation ends. I was never XXXX billing cycles behind after forbearance, so a XXXX delinquency can not be supported. 

I have asked XXXX XXXX to explain how the forbearance months were handled and to provide documentation supporting their reporting method. They have not provided this information and have only repeated general statements that the reporting is accurate, without addressing the specific issue. 

I am requesting : Removal of all inaccurate XXXX delinquencies. 

Correction of all forbearance-covered months to current, as required by XXXX XXXX XXXX. 

Reporting only the actual delinquency that occurred after the forbearance ended ( closer to 3060 days, not XXXX ). 

Consistent reporting across all three bureaus. 

This inaccurate reporting is causing significant credit harm, and I am requesting CFPB assistance to correct it.

CFPB REBUTTAL National Credit Systems ( NCS ) Continues to Furnish Without Legal Authority This is my formal rebuttal to National Credit Systems response. NCS has failed to provide any legally required documentation demonstrating that they have authority to furnish, verify, or collect the alleged apartment debt reported on my consumer report.

1. NCS provided only original landlord documents that do NOT authorize them to report The documents NCS sent to the CFPB are : A lease agreement between XXXXYES Communities and the tenant ( dated XX/XX/year> ). 
Nowhere in this lease is there any clause authorizing the landlord OR any third-party collector to report rental information to consumer reporting agencies. 

XXXX A move-out comparison report showing alleged damages and charges.

XXXX A ledger showing monthly rent charges and payments created by the landlords internal system. 
The ledger contains NO reference to NCS and NO evidence of any transfer or assignment to NCS. 

XXXX None of the documents supplied prove that NCS has ANY ownership interest or authorization to furnish consumer credit information. 

2. NCS admits it is a third-party collector, but provided no servicing agreement NCS states : National Credit Systems , Inc. is a third-party debt collection agency collecting a debt on behalf of XXXX. 

If NCS is a servicer, they must provide a written servicing agreement expressly granting them the right to : furnish data verify ACDVs report to XXXX access consumer reports collect on behalf of Deerhurst NCS provided none of these documents.

3. NCS has no permissible purpose to furnish under the FCRA Under 15 U.S.C. 1681b ( f ) and 1681b ( a ), a furnisher must have BOTH : a permissible purpose AND authorization from the creditor Since the lease contains no reporting clause, XXXX never had consumer consent to report. Therefore, XXXX can not delegate authority they never had, and NCS has no permissible purpose at all.

4. NCS violated FCRA 623 and 1681s-2 ( b ) After I disputed the account with the CRAs, NCS was required to : verify using actual documentation ; OR delete the tradeline.

Since NCS has no assignment, no servicing contract, no authorization to furnish, and no ownership interest, any verification transmitted to a CRA constitutes : FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) furnishing inaccurate/unverifiable information FCRA 1681s-2 ( b ) failure to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation 5. NCS violated the FDCPA By continuing to represent that they have authority to collect and report this debt when they do not, NCS violated : FDCPA 1692e ( 2 ) ( A ) false representation of the character or legal status of a debt FDCPA 1692e ( 8 ) communicating or threatening to communicate false credit information FDCPA 1692f unfair and unauthorized collection practices 6. Required resolution Because NCS has failed to produce : a Contract of Assignment a Bill of Sale identifying the account a Servicing Agreement written authorization to furnish proof of permissible purpose I request : Immediate deletion of the National Credit Systems tradeline from all consumer reporting agencies.

If NCS continues furnishing without lawful authority, I will proceed with federal litigation under : FCRA 1681n, 1681o FDCPA 1692k all applicable state consumer protection statutes This constitutes my full rebuttal and request for enforcement. Consider this final demand and I will litigate in federal court immediately

Details of the Problem Fifth Third notified me of an escrow shortage, which increased my monthly mortgage payment. I pay automatically, and because of the change, my payment was short by approximately {$27.00}. 

Instead of applying the payment and notifying me of the shortfall, Fifth Third refused to apply the payment, marked it as late, and charged a late fee. This alone is troubling, given how minor the shortage was and that it resulted entirely from their own escrow recalculation. 

However, what happened next raised far more serious concerns.

Their representative told me that the number was NOT associated with Fifth Third and that it was a fraudulent number. 

However, after further review, it appears that this number is, in fact, used by Fifth Thirds own automated collections department to notify customers about delinquent payments. This directly contradicts what their representative told me.

This is significant misinformation whether intentional or not.

Consumers searching the number online are also led to believe it is a scam, including via results connected to Fifth Thirds own fraud-alert pages.

Fifth Third then uses this same number to call customers about late payments caused by their escrow adjustments, while simultaneously charging fees when payments are short by small amounts. 

The confusion surrounding this phone number makes it extremely difficult for consumers to distinguish legitimate contact from actual fraud, which increases both financial and security risks. 

Given how much revenue financial institutions generate from late fees, it is difficult not to question whether this confusing setup misinformation about valid numbers and refusal to apply near-full payments could create conditions that disproportionately benefit the bank at the consumers expense. 

I am not claiming a proven intention, but the pattern is highly suspicious and warrants investigation.

An explanation of why I was explicitly told by Fifth Third that the number was fraudulent when evidence indicates it is in their system. 

A review of the banks escrow recalculation notifications, short-payment handling, and late fee practices.

Assurance that consumers are not being misled or placed at financial risk due to contradictory or false information provided by the bank.

The account is being reported with materially inconsistent and misleading information, including but not limited to conflicting dates, improper account status, failure to accurately reflect transfer or sale of the account, and failure to report the account as disputed across consumer reporting agencies. 
Supporting authorities include : Cushman v. Trans Union, 115 F.3d 220 ( 3d Cir. 1997 ) CRAs and furnishers must conduct a reasonable investigation and can not merely parrot prior reporting ; Saunders v. BB & T, 526 F.3d 142 ( 4th Cir. 2008 ) failure to report a bona fide dispute is materially misleading ; Gorman v. Wolpoff & Abramson, 584 F.3d 1147 ( 9th Cir. 2009 ) furnishers are liable for failure to investigate and correct inaccurate information after notice ; Dennis v. BEH-1, LLC, 520 F.3d 1066 ( 9th Cir. 2008 ) accuracy and reasonableness are jury questions where conflicting records exist. 
As shown in the attached highlighted credit-report screenshots, the tradeline contains internal inconsistencies such as : Conflicting Dates of First Delinquency and Date Reported across bureaus ; Reporting a collection or charge-off status while simultaneously reflecting a zero balance or inactive status ; Failure to properly reflect transfer or sale using correct Account Status and Special Comment codes under XXXX XXXX standards ; Failure to apply the XB dispute code during an active investigation.

Absolute Resolutions Investment, LLC is attempting to collect an alleged debt from me without providing legally required validation, proof of ownership, or evidence of contractual obligation. Despite my formal request for debt verification, the company failed to supply competent evidence that the account is valid, that they own the debt, or that I agreed to any contract with the original creditor. 

This conduct violates multiple provisions of federal law and constitutes unlawful debt collection activity, inaccurate credit reporting, and failure to comply with statutory verification duties. 
Violation of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) Absolute Resolutions Investment failed to provide proper debt validation after receiving my dispute. Under federal law, a debt collector must cease all collection activity until verification is mailed to the consumer.

They did not provide : A copy of the original signed agreement or contract Evidence I agreed to the debt Proof they lawfully purchased or were assigned the account A complete itemized accounting of the balance Proof the alleged debt is still legally enforceable Continuing collection without validation is an explicit statutory violation.

Violation of 15 U.S.C. 1692e Absolute Resolutions Investment has misrepresented : The legal status of the alleged debt Their right to collect it The accuracy of reported amounts The existence of a valid contractual obligation Reporting or collecting without proof constitutes deceptive conduct under federal law.

Violation of 15 U.S.C. 1692f Attempting to collect an unverified debt with no evidence of ownership or obligation is an unfair and unconscionable collection practice.

Violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) and ( b ) Absolute Resolutions Investment furnished information to consumer reporting agencies without verifying accuracy and failed to conduct a lawful investigation after dispute.

This violates : The duty to report only accurate information The duty to investigate disputed data The duty to delete unverifiable information If information can not be validated, it must be removed by law.

Violation of FDCPA and Common-Law Assignment Principles A debt buyer must show : A valid chain of custody A bill of sale naming the account Proof of assignment from original creditor No such proof has been provided. Without ownership, Absolute Resolutions Investment has no legal standing to collect or report.

Failure to comply constitutes : Continued violations of federal law Exposure to statutory damages Exposure to actual damages Exposure to attorney 's fees and court costs under 15 U.S.C. 1692k and 15 U.S.C. 1681n/o

narrative:
I am filing a complaint regarding PayPals improper handling of a transaction dispute involving digital goods.

I operate a business PayPal account under an EIN. A customer filed an Item Not Received ( INR ) claim for digital goods, which by nature do not involve physical shipment or carrier tracking. Despite this, PayPal evaluated the dispute using physical-goods delivery standards. 

I provided clear evidence during the dispute process showing successful digital delivery, including access provision, delivery confirmation, and usage indicators. This evidence was uploaded prior to the case closure. PayPal nonetheless ruled in favor of the buyer, citing inability to confirm delivery, which is not an appropriate standard for digital transactions. 

As a result, PayPal refunded the buyer and placed a negative balance of approximately {$2500.00} on my business account. This decision was made without proper consideration of the evidence provided and without acknowledging that INR claims are frequently misapplied to digital goods.

I am requesting that PayPal : 1. Conduct a manual supervisory review of the dispute, 2. Reevaluate the evidence submitted under standards applicable to digital delivery, 3. Reverse the improper debit or otherwise resolve the balance fairly, and 4. Cease any collection activity related to this disputed amount while the matter is under review.

This issue represents a systemic problem in how PayPal handles digital-goods disputes and exposes sellers to buyer misuse of INR claims.This is incredibly discouraging to young entrepreneurs and small businesses especially in the digital, online, and marketing communities. I am requesting CFPB assistance to ensure the dispute is reviewed fairly and in accordance with the nature of the transaction.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

I am submitting this complaint regarding Synchrony Banks failure to provide reasonable consumer access to historical credit card statements for my TJX Rewards Mastercard account, despite repeated confirmation that such records exist within its internal systems. 

In XX/XX/XXXX, all of my personal and financial records were destroyed in the XXXX XXXX fire. Since that time, I have successfully reconstructed records through multiple financial institutions by retrieving archived statements. Synchrony is the only institution that has been unable to fulfill what should be a routine archival request.

When I accessed Synchronys online portal, only approximately one year of statements was available. Following Synchronys customer-service guidance, I submitted the appropriate online requests for older records and undertook extensive follow-up. To date, I have spoken with no fewer than eight Synchrony representatives and spent multiple hours attempting to resolve this issue.

These calls were preceded by earlier efforts through Synchronys website and online request system.

Across these interactions, Synchrony representatives consistently confirmed that my historical statements are visible within internal systems. However, I was advised that system limitations prevent digital delivery of more than a minimal subset of historical statementsdescribed verbally as three statementsdespite the records existing electronically.

I reviewed Synchronys publicly available cardholder agreements, paperless statement disclosures, and consumer-facing FAQs and found no published policy, contractual provision, or disclosure imposing a numeric limit on digital delivery of historical statements or requiring that archived statements be provided only in paper form. Absent a disclosed policy, this limitation appears to be an internal system or tooling constraint rather than a consumer-facing rule.

After weeks of effort, I received only three statements from XXXX. In an attempt to prevent recurrence, I requested statements dating back to XXXX. That request appears to have surfaced a deeper systems issue. I subsequently received correspondence indicating that no statements exist for XXXX or for the years XXXXa factually incorrect assertion. I was advised that this issue stems from incorrect or prior card numbers being associated with those years within Synchronys systems, resulting in failed retrievals.

From a process, systems, and governance standpoint, this reflects a breakdown between record retention, customer-facing platforms, and escalation authority. While individual representatives were professional and courteous, they were constrained by tools and policies that prevented resolution. As a result, I have been unable to obtain complete records that Synchrony confirms it maintains.

I am requesting the CFPBs assistance in ensuring that Synchrony provides reasonable consumer access to retained account records and resolves the apparent system-mapping and delivery failures described above.

I am submitting this complaint against TransUnion LLC for repeatedly failing and refusing to conduct a lawful investigation into my credit report disputes, despite my full compliance with all identity verification requirements under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). 

I have mailed multiple written dispute letters to TransUnion, including my most recent dispute dated XX/XX/year>, in which I clearly identified inaccurate, incomplete, and inconsistent information appearing on my consumer credit report. Along with my dispute, I properly enclosed all required identity verification documentation, including government-issued identification, proof of address, and signed correspondence, sufficient to verify my identity and confirm that I am the consumer submitting the dispute. 

Despite these efforts, TransUnion has continuously failed and refused to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation as required by FCRA 611 ( 15 U.S.C. 1681i ). Instead of completing an investigation within the statutory timeframe, TransUnion has ignored my disputes and effectively stonewalled my lawful requests, depriving me of my consumer rights. 

TransUnions failure to investigate is particularly egregious because the disputed items include accounts, collections, inquiries, and personal information that are inaccurate, inconsistent, or reported with material discrepancies, all of which are clearly outlined in my attached dispute letter. These inaccuracies are causing ongoing harm to my credit profile and financial standing. 

Under the FCRA, once a consumer submits a dispute with sufficient identifying information, a credit reporting agency must conduct a reasonable reinvestigation and either verify, correct, or delete the disputed information. TransUnions continued refusal to do so constitutes a willful and negligent violation of federal law, including but not limited to : FCRA 611 ( a ) Failure to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation FCRA 607 ( b ) Failure to maintain reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy FCRA 609 & 610 Failure to properly handle consumer disclosures and disputes

Unauthorized Hard Inquiries TransUnion is reporting multiple hard inquiries that I did not authorize. Given my documented identity-theft status and trafficking-related identity compromise, any inquiry lacking strict proof of permissible purpose must be deleted or blocked. 

I requested the Method of Verification ( MOV ) for each inquiry, including permissible-purpose codes, member numbers, signed authorizations, and device/IP logs where applicable. To date, TransUnion has failed to provide competent verification.

I am submitting this complaint to dispute the actions of a debt collection agency, Credit Collection Services, for violations of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) and the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). 

On XX/XX/year>, I received a collection notice from Credit Collection Services by mail for the first time regarding an alleged debt. 

On XX/XX/year>, within the XXXX validation period provided under federal law, I mailed a written debt validation request to Credit Collection Services XXXX 

Credit Collection Services failed to respond to my debt validation request and did not provide any verification or documentation substantiating the alleged debt. 

Instead, after receiving my validation request, the company reported the collection account to the credit reporting agencies without first validating the debt. 

Violations of Federal Law Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) Under the FDCPA, once a consumer timely disputes a debt and requests validation, a debt collector must cease all collection activity until the debt has been properly verified. Reporting a disputed debt to the credit bureaus constitutes continued collection activity. By adding this account to my credit report without first validating the debt, Credit Collection Services violated this provision.

Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) & ( b ) The FCRA requires furnishers of information to ensure that information reported to consumer reporting agencies is accurate and verified. Furnishing an unverified and disputed debt to the credit bureaus is inaccurate and misleading. Additionally, failing to note the account as disputed further violates the FCRA. 

Harm Caused to My Credit Profile The improper reporting of this unverified collection account has caused, and continues to cause, harm to my credit profile, including but not limited to : Potential and actual credit score reduction Increased difficulty obtaining credit, housing, or favorable interest rates Damage to my overall creditworthiness and financial reputation Emotional distress resulting from inaccurate and unlawful credit reporting This harm is especially concerning given that the debt was timely disputed and never validated as required by law.

I am submitting this complaint against Experian Information Solutions XXXX XXXX for repeated failures to maintain accurate personal identifying information on my consumer credit report, despite multiple disputes submitted online and by telephone. 

Although the street name is spelled correctly, Experian repeatedly reports my address without my apartment number, which renders the address incomplete, inaccurate, and misleading in a multi-unit residential complex. 

Repeated Disputes & Pattern of Reinsertion I have disputed this issue : Multiple times online Multiple times by phone with Experian representatives During phone disputes, I was advised that both versions of the address were removed. However, Experian later re-added the incorrect address without the apartment number, often alongside the correct address. 

Each time the correct address is added, the incomplete address is also reintroduced without notice, explanation, or identification of the reporting source. 

Failure to Notify & Account-Level Inaccuracies Experian fails to : Notify me when the incorrect address is reinserted Identify which furnisher or account caused the reinsertion Ensure consistency of identifying information across accounts As a result, my credit report continues to reflect inaccurate personal information, undermining the integrity and reliability of the report. 

Resulting Harm & Inaccuracy of the Credit Report Because Experian continues to report an incomplete and inaccurate address : My credit report does not meet the FCRA standard of maximum possible accuracy The report may be used by lenders, insurers, or other parties based on incorrect identifying data I have been forced to repeatedly dispute the same issue, causing unnecessary time, effort, and stress This ongoing inaccuracy has materially compromised the accuracy of my consumer report. 

Violations of Federal Law Experians conduct violates multiple provisions of the Fair Credit Reporting Act, including but not limited to : 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) Failure to follow reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) Failure to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation after disputes ( including phone disputes ) 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ) ( A ) Failure to correct or delete information that can not be verified as accurate 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ) ( B ) Improper reinsertion of disputed information without appropriate safeguards or notice Request for CFPB Action & Compensation Review I respectfully request that the CFPB require Experian to : Permanently remove the incomplete address lacking the apartment number Ensure that only the accurate address below appears on my credit file : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Identify and correct any account-level reporting that continues to reintroduce the inaccurate address Provide written confirmation of all corrections Review whether Experians repeated failures and improper reinsertion practices warrant compensation or other relief, as allowed under the FCRA If Experian is unable to maintain accurate personal identifying information after repeated disputes, the continued reporting of inaccurate data should be considered willful or negligent noncompliance, subject to applicable remedies under 15 U.S.C. 1681n and 1681o. Thank you for your attention to this matter and for enforcing consumer protections under federal law.

Summary: XXXX XXXX Comenity denied my XXXX XXXX XXXX  application citing only inability to verify your previous credit experience. The notice failed to state specific principal reasons under ECOA/Reg B and failed to provide lawful FCRA score disclosures (claimed score XXXX XXXX XXXX  despite stating the decision was based on a consumer report. Legal basis: ECOA (15 U.S.C. 1691 & Reg B 1002.9)  failure to provide specific principal reasons; FCRA (15 U.S.C. 1681m & Reg V)  defective score disclosure and factor disclosure

[What happened]
On December 19, 2024 Comenity Capital Bank sent an adverseaction letter denying my XXXX  Visa Signature application. The letter stated only: Inability to verify your previous credit experience. It also included a purported credit score disclosure that said the score was not able to be calculated and listed a score range of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXhile simultaneously stating the decision was based on information in my consumer report.

Why this is a problem

Under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Regulation B a creditor must provide a written adverseaction notice that either (a) states the specific principal reason(s) for denial or (b) informs the applicant of the right to request those reasons; the notice must identify principal creditworthiness factors, not vague internal process failures. Comenitys single phrase is vague, nonspecific, and appears to describe an internal verification failure rather than a consumer creditworthiness factor.

Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act and Regulation V, when an adverse action is based in whole or in part on a consumer report the creditor must disclose the numerical credit score used (if any), the score range, the date of the score, the key factors affecting the score, the CRA name and contact information, and notice of the right to obtain a free report within 60 days. Comenitys XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  and was not able to be calculated statement are nonsensical and inconsistent with its statement that the decision was based on a consumer report. The listed most significant factors repeat the same vague phrase and do not identify score factors.

Steps I took  
I mailed a demand letter by certified mail requesting corrected disclosures and a compliant adverseaction notice. Certified mail tracking number XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX4 shows delivery to Comenity Capital Bank in XXXX, OH on XXXX XXXX XXXX  I have attached the original denial letter, my demand letter, and USPS delivery confirmation.

Requested action from CFPB  
I request that the CFPB investigate whether Comenity Capital Bank violated ECOA/Regulation B and FCRA/Regulation V by issuing a deficient adverseaction notice and defective credit score disclosure, and require Comenity to provide the corrective disclosures and other relief listed below.'

As such, any transaction or experience between myself and XXXX XXXX XXXX regarding this account should not be included in my consumer credit report.

Proof of Compliance with 15 U.S. Code 1637 ( b ) : I request documentation showing that the periodic statement, containing all required information, was mailed or delivered to me at least 21 days before the payment due date. 
Detailed Documentation : Under 15 U.S. Code 1637 ( b ), specific information must be included in the periodic statement. Please provide documentation that proves the statement was issued in compliance with these requirements and was delivered within the legal timeframe. 
Notice of Requirements : In accordance with Rule 1002, you are required to provide me with the requested documentation within 10 calendar days of receiving this notice. 
Please be advised that merely asserting the information is accurate is not sufficient. 
Without clear proof of compliance with the relevant provisions of the FCRA ( specifically 15 U.S. Code 1681a ( 2 ) ( A ) ( i ), 1666b, and 1637 ( b ) ), the information reported to the credit bureau is invalid, and there is no basis for it to remain on my credit report.

I did not authorize these transactions, nor did I authorize any individual, device, or digital wallet to use my card or account credentials.

The transactions occurred at multiple locations in different regions, which is inconsistent with cardholder presence or authorization.

I can provide documentary proof of my work schedule and presence if requested. I did not provision my debit card to any device other than my own, and I did not authorize tokenized or digital wallet use. Additionally, M & T Bank relied heavily on financial and technical jargon ( including terms such as token usage, authorized, and properly processed ) without providing clear, plain-language explanations of how these terms established consumer authorization. issue: Problem with a company's investigation into an existing problem
sub_issue: Their investigation did not fix an error on your report
narrative:
I am submitting this as a new complaint based on Experians failure to comply with federal and Washington State law after notice through a prior CFPB complaint. Although Experian acknowledged my prior submission and repeatedly characterized it as a dispute submitted through the CFPB Complaint Portal, its response failed to demonstrate that a reasonable reinvestigation was conducted. 

Experian relied on generalized statements that entities certified a permissible purpose to access my credit report. Certification alone does not constitute verification. Experian did not provide documentation establishing lawful authorization for each disputed inquiry, including signed applications, digital consent, or dealer finance agreements, as required under FCRA 604 ( a ). Experian also failed to identify the specific furnishers or public data sources relied upon to retain disputed inquiries or outdated personal identifiers. Without identifying sources or producing evidence, Experian can not demonstrate maximum possible accuracy as required by FCRA 607 ( b ) and RCW 19.182.110 ( 1 ). 

Experian further failed to disclose the results of any reinvestigation, including what information was reviewed, which furnishers were contacted, what documentation ( if any ) was obtained, or how accuracy was confirmed. This constitutes non-compliance with FCRA 611 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) and FCRA 611 ( a ) ( 6 ) ( B ), as well as RCW 19.182.070, which require reasonable reinvestigation and disclosure of verification results. 

Instead of responding substantively to the issues raised, Experian redirected me to its private dispute portal. Consumers are not legally required to use a credit bureaus internal website to dispute inaccurate or incomplete information. Having elected to treat my CFPB submission as a dispute, Experian can not reclassify it as a customer-service inquiry in order to avoid its statutory obligations under federal or state law. 

Experians response explains how inquiries may generally be reported but does not address whether the specific disputed inquiries and personal identifiers on my file were lawfully obtained, accurately reported, or properly verified. A generalized explanation of policy does not resolve a consumer dispute and does not satisfy the Fair Credit Reporting Act or Washington State law.

Experians handling of this matter reflects a broader process failure in which consumer disputes are unnecessarily diverted, delayed, or complicated rather than substantively investigated. By relying on boilerplate explanations, redirecting consumers between portals, and withholding source-level verification, Experian creates procedural friction that discourages consumers from pursuing their lawful rights. This approach appears designed to promote consumer attrition while protecting the credit bureaus own operational interests, rather than ensuring compliance with the accuracy, transparency, and reinvestigation requirements mandated by law. 

The Fair Credit Reporting Act does not permit credit reporting agencies to complicate the dispute process, delay resolution, or rely on consumer exhaustion as a substitute for compliance. Such practices frustrate the statutes purpose and undermine the consumer protections established by Congress and Washington State law. 

Because Experian failed to identify sources, failed to provide documentation, failed to disclose reinvestigation results, and failed to demonstrate that any reasonable investigative steps were taken after notice, Experian remains in non-compliance with FCRA 604 ( a ), 607 ( b ), 611 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ), and 611 ( a ) ( 6 ) ( B ), as well as RCW 19.182.070 and RCW 19.182.110 ( 1 ).

I am requesting regulatory review and appropriate corrective action to require Experian to correct its dispute-handling process and to delete any information that can not be fully verified in compliance with federal and Washington State law

narrative:
I entered into a retail deferred-interest promotional financing agreement provided by Synchrony Bank for a XXXX XXXX purchase in the amount of {$6600.00}, with a 24-month promotional period, as documented in the attached sales and financing agreement dated XX/XX/year>. 

The written agreement states that no interest will be assessed if the promotional balance is paid in full within the promotional period, and that if it is not paid in full, interest will be imposed retroactively from the date of purchase at an APR of 34.99 %. The agreement also states that minimum monthly payments are required. 

Critically, the agreement does not disclose that early payments or payments in excess of the minimum may fail to satisfy minimum payment requirements, nor does it disclose that payments made prior to the first billing statement may be treated differently or excluded from satisfying the minimum payment obligation.

Prior to receiving my first billing statement, I made an early payment of approximately {$400.00} toward the account. I also scheduled recurring bi-weekly electronic payments that would have resulted in approximately {$600.00} paid before the first payment due date of XX/XX/XXXX. 

Despite having paid nearly three times the stated minimum payment before the due date, I learned that Synchrony would still consider the account late if a separate {$210.00} minimum payment was not credited within a specific billing window. Under this structure, a consumer can pay early, pay extra, and still be deemed late solely due to internal payment classification rules that are not disclosed in the written agreement. 

Had this occurred, my promotional 0 % financing would have been converted into a penalty APR of up to 39.99 %, with interest applied retroactively to the original purchase date. 

A reasonable consumer reviewing the attached agreement would believe that paying early and paying more than the minimum would protect them from late fees and penalty interest. The omission of how early payments are applied and how they may fail to satisfy minimum payment requirements creates a substantial risk of consumer harm and appears designed to trigger deferred interest despite responsible payment behavior. 

I believe this constitutes an unfair and deceptive practice, based on material omissions in the written disclosures and the unreasonable expectation that consumers anticipate undisclosed payment-application rules.

Regulation E Violations Bank Failed to Provide Required Documentation and Failed to Issue Provisional Credit. 

This complaint is not about the original dispute, but about SoFi Banks repeated violations of Regulation E during the dispute process. The bank did not follow the requirements of 12 CFR 1005.11 and denied my rights under EFTA.

1. SoFi did not provide the documents they used in their investigation.

Violation : 12 CFR 1005.11 ( d ) I asked twice for the documents they relied on to deny my dispute, and they still have not provided anything. Regulation E requires the bank to give the consumer copies of the documents they used. Without this, I can not verify whether their investigation was valid.

2. SoFi failed to issue provisional credit for one of the transactions.

Violation : 12 CFR 1005.11 ( c ) ( 2 ) ( i ) The {$800.00} dispute was not resolved within 10 business days, and they never issued provisional credit. Regulation E requires provisional credit when the investigation is not completed in time. This requirement is not optional.

3. SoFi used the fact that my card was in my possession to deny the claim, which is not allowed.

Violation : 12 CFR 1005.2 ( m ) Regulation E makes it clear that a transaction can be unauthorized even if the card is in the consumers possession. SoFi treated card-present as proof of authorization, which is not legally correct.

4. The bank tried to restart the Regulation E timeline by asking for additional information after they had already made a decision. 
Violation : 12 CFR 1005.11 ( c ) ( 1 ) The clock for the investigation starts when the consumer reports the error. The bank can not extend or reset the timeline by requesting unnecessary information after an initial decision. This delayed the investigation and delayed provisional credit.

5. They changed the dispute type without my consent.

Violation : 12 CFR 1005.11 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( ii ) Expecting to be charged {$100.00} does not authorize {$150.00}. SoFi reclassified my dispute based on my explanation, but that does not change the fact that the higher amount was not authorized.

6. SoFis investigation was not reasonable.

Violation : 12 CFR 1005.11 ( c ) ( 1 ) Rather than provide actual evidence, they referenced irrelevant facts like me logging into my account days before the transaction. That does not prove authorization or resolve whether an error occurred. A reasonable investigation requires reviewing merchant data and transaction evidence, which they did not provide. 

I raised these issues in a prior complaint, but the bank still refuses to provide documentation or issue provisional credit. I am filing this new complaint specifically for the Regulation E violations listed above. 

I am requesting that the CFPB require SoFi Bank to : Provide all documentation relied upon in their investigation Issue full provisional credit for both disputed transactions as required Reinvestigate the matter in compliance with Regulation E Because these issues involve repeated violations of Regulation E, the failure to provide required documentation, and the failure to issue mandatory provisional credit under 1005.11 ( c ) ( 2 ) ( i ), I am asking for supervisory escalation of this complaint. I have attempted to resolve this matter directly with the bank, and the previous CFPB complaint did not result in compliance. These violations continue to cause financial harm, and the bank has not followed federal requirements. I am requesting that this complaint be reviewed at the supervisory level for enforcement of Regulation E. 

Thank you.
